body: Tales of Xillia is Namco Tales Studio's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan in September 2011. Jude Mathis and Milla Maxwell become fugitives after interfering with the Lance of Kresnik, a weapon threatening the relationship between humans and spirits. The player chooses a lead viewpoint, following a party whose members arrive with different commitments and experiences. Exploration moves into active battles, while conversations between the group give the journey a more personal rhythm. The story's larger conflict is carried through the relationship between two protagonists who understand their responsibility in different ways.

The battle system lets party members form links that provide support and lead into coordinated actions. A character's immediate attacks therefore belong to a relationship with somebody else on the field. The player changes the pairing to suit the encounter, considering both the controlled fighter and the assistance available around them. Outside battle, voiced skits give companions room to react to events and one another. These smaller exchanges help make the group more than a collection of combat roles, connecting the practical cooperation of a fight to the personalities travelling together between encounters.

Kōsuke Fujishima and Mutsumi Inomata both contributed character designs, bringing together artists closely associated with different parts of Tales. Motoi Sakuraba composed the music, while Naoto Miyadera directed and Hideo Baba produced. Western editions arrived in August 2013 after a strong Japanese reception and substantial sales. A direct sequel followed in Japan in 2012, and a later remaster returned the original adventure to more platforms. Xillia's defining contribution is the pairing at its centre, expressed through both the story's viewpoints and a combat system that makes one fighter's actions more useful through another.
